EICMA 2026 • Triumph TF-E Bikes Get Even More Enduro With Updates for the 2027 Model Year
23 New Kaido House, Mini GT, Pop Race and Tarmac Works Collectibles for November 2026
54 photos
Photo: Kaido House
Just a few days ago I unboxed 10 Hot Wheels cars that were a real bargain. Some might say they’re genuine peg-warmers, but that perspective might not be valid a few years from now. My next story will include 10 Ferraris from Mattel but I’m planing to do something different during the final days of November.
I will be comparing Hot Wheels collectibles to products from other manufacturers. I thought I was all set to go for that story, as I had already bought a Car Culture 2-Pack for the job.
However, I figured the Kaido House, Mini GT and Ixo models were individually worth as much as the 2-pack, which wasn’t entirely fair. So, I decided to upgrade and give Mattel an equal fighting chance by picking up two Elite 64 items.
I’ve only previously bought the Porsche 993 GT2 from that series, and I can tell you there’s another Porsche on the new list, too.
Now, I’m just giving you a preview of what’s coming this month, and I’d like to focus on some of the newest 1/64th-scale pre-orders on the market next. You could pay as much as $500 for all these, so it might be smarter to just purchase the ones you’re the most excited about.
Kaido House Photo: Kaido House I feel like I have been ignoring Jun Imai’s project for too long. I imagine Kaido House was his opportunity to build the tiny cars he loved the most, on a more premium level than he ever could with Hot Wheels.
The company has been around since 2021, and has released several amazing castings since. The latest pre-order includes four models, which could be ready to ship out by Q2 of 2027. The Nissan Skyline GT-R (R32) was the first of two that I wanted to sign up for.
It’s not just because this is my favorite generation of the GT-R, but also because of the Advan livery. I can only recall seeing three previous variations of it, and neither was remotely as good as this one. The other model I might buy is the fictional Kaido Star sporting that wild bosozoku/kaido racer look.
The moment I laid eyes on it I had an instant flashback of some dioramas and similar cars I saw at the Tokyo Auto Salon back in 2016. I don’t think I’d ever like to build a car like this in the real world, but having a tiny version of it at home is one way to recognize a special part of Japanese car culture.
Photo: Kaido House I just hope it won’t be a slippery slope towards getting an unreasonable number of them next. I believe the Lancia Delta HF Integrale is a brand new casting for Kaido House, and it’s a surprising appearance to say the least.
Mr. Imai hasn’t focused solely on Japanese machines so far, as we’ve seen some American cars in the mix. But Lancia is the last car manufacturer I expected to see from Mini GT’s partner brand.
The removable magnetic hood adds a nice touch to an already iconic design, and the red and white color combo is seriously enticing.
The pink finish on the Chevrolet Camaro immediately reminded me of Ken Block’s Hoonipigasus , although the design’s origins are much older than that. It’s an interesting machine for sure, and the twin-turbo engine is the main attraction here.
Mini GT Photo: Mini GT As far as I can tell, the “official”, final Mini GT preorder for November should go live on either the 23rd or the 24th. The last time we had one I had just realized the diecast manufacturer posts a new one every two weeks.
That hasn’t stopped the team from coming out with some special releases in between, and this time both Peanuts and James Bond fans will be pretty happy about the update.
Let’s start with with the two race spec GT-Rs. Snoopy is on the #23 car, while Woodstock is on the #24 racer.
The blue Nissan GT-R NISMO GT3 gets two card variations, as one was a special item for Mini GT’s Yokohama Pop Up Store.
Photo: Mini GT There’s also a paper bag included in the offer if you buy both cars, while supplies last. It’s not something I will be pursuing, but I imagine many fans of the franchise will want a closer look.
The 007 collection seems to have become an important part of the strategy, and I think there are currently 10 items in the pre-order phase.
Think of the Aston Martin DBS (Casino Royale), the Land Rover Defender 110 Crew Cab (Skyfall) or the Aston Martin V12 Vanquish (Die Another Day) to name a few). Now, for me James Bond began with Pierce Brosnan, so I’m not familiar with any of the movies that preceded him.
Seeing the new Mini GT Tuk Tuk (Octopussy) and AMC Hornet X Hatchback (The Man with the Golden Gun) makes me think I should give Roger Moore a chance soon.
Pop Race Photo: Pop Race Now, I am little late in reporting on two of the models here, as the pre-order session closes on November 23rd. I just hope this story reaches you in due time, but even if it doesn’t it shouldn’t be impossible to get ahold of these next year.
The LB Works Supra A90 is a brand new casting for Pop Race , and it doesn’t really mean anything to me. I guess it’s proof that most of the brand’s clients are quite a bit younger than I am. Otherwise, I’d expect more variations of the old Supra. And I don’t just mean the GT300 model that I enjoyed unboxing in July.
The Touge Maou is one of the most iconic versions of the Honda S2000 ever made, at least if you consumed as much as of Hot Version as I did growing up. The J’s Racing version of the car makes the Pandem S2000 look almost boring by comparison, but I might be biased in saying that. I think Pop Race is slightly late to the party though, as Inno64 must have had a tiny replica of this car for at least a year now.
Come to think of it, neither one of my local dealers advertised the pre-order for this car. It’s either that or I completely forgot about it, which is why I know who I’ll be calling the moment I’m done writing this story. Everyone seems to be jumping onboard the 7-Eleven bandwagon these days, so the Mercedes-AMG GT3 EVO should come as no surprise. I’ve had enough of this car already!
Tarmac Works Photo: Tarmac Works If you’ve read my interview with Felix Kwong (the man who created Tarmac Works over a decade ago), you’ll know he has a personal connection to the Macau Grand Prix. That said, it’s no wonder his brand is always onsite for some sort of project or new release.
The Pompompurin-themed Mercedes-AMG GT3 will be available both as a 1/64th and 1/43rd scale collectible at the 73rd edition of the event. The same goes for three more race cars on this list: the #11 Porsche 911 GT3 R driven by Ayhancan Guven, the #22 GT3 R driven by Laurin Heinrich, and also the #79 Mercedes-AMG GT4.
If you’re at the race, you might even find Maro Engel’s Initial D-themed Mercedes in the vending machines! For me, pre-ordering one of the eight models in the official pre-order session is a much more accessible option.
The LB-Works Nissan GT-R R35 type 2 is the latest “Tuner & Street” collectible, and it could trigger some nostalgia for those of us who loved 2 Fast 2 Furious.
Photo: Tarmac Works I confess I had no clue that Jorge Lorenzo competed in the Porsche Carrera Cup, but that’s not a good enough reason for me to buy this car as I’m not fond of the color combo.
It couldn’t have been that long ago that we saw a green variation of the Bentley Continental GT3: the new one is a throwback to the 2019 edition of 24 Hours at Spa.
The BMW M4 GT3 and the Porsche 911 Carrera 4 GTS are the two Minichamps Exclusives in this pre-order, and I plan to skip both of them and the Audi Quattro A2 Gr.B Rally car for something else. The Ferrari F355 Challenge looks great in Silver, which isn’t something I will often say.
Meanwhile, the yellow F40 GTE is simply out of this world. And it’s slightly funny knowing I have a similar Hot Wheels collectible with a special feature coming right up.
